name: Malua Bay
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Wessels, Kanauhea. 2013. Malua Bay: A description of the Malua Bay language (Malekula, Vanuatu). MA thesis, University of Waikato. PDF from Waikato Research Commons.
catalog_quote: Stress is not phonemically contrastive in Malua Bay. Auditory analysis, using Transcriber, found that stress in disyllabic (3.48), trisyllabic (3.49), and polysyllabic (3.50) lexemes falls syllable-initially unless there is a mid central vowel /ə/ occupying the first syllable, whereby stress then falls on the next syllable that does not contain the /ə/ phoneme. If however the morpheme only contains the mid central vowel at the syllable nucleus (nuclei), stress falls on the first syllable (3.51). (3.48) /ʹa.xon/ 'here' ... /mə.'ne/ 'can, able' ... /ʹʧa.ləŋ/ 'outside' ... /pə.pə.ʹkak/ 'chicken cackle' ... /sə.sə.ʹre/ 'learn' (3.49) /ʹwer.wer.ik/ 'small, tiny' ... /sə.ʹŋa.vəl/ 'ten' /ʹvex.pə.rev/ 'soon' ... /tər.tə.ʹra/ 'old, mature' (3.50) /rə.ʹne.si.sax/ 'rice' /pə.ʹri.ri.rev/ 'long' /ʹpu.ni.xə.wen/ 'six days ago' /nə.ʹxar.xar.ən/ 'love' (3.51) /ʹrə.lən/ 'egg' /ʹxə.ʧə.rəx/ 'sneeze'

audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim at the stated locator (sec. 3.3, pp. 59-60, exx. 3.48-3.51) in the held Wessels 2013 thesis text. The classification (quality-sensitive 'weight', full-vs-reduced-vowel, leftmost full vowel else initial, unbounded, no secondary stress described, non-contrastive) matches the source statement and its examples. Wessels 2013 is Glottolog's top-ranked (grammar, 208 pp) and only Malua Bay description; no later phonology, JIPA illustration, or instrumental study was found in the Waikato repository or Glottolog, and the 2018 LDD Language Contexts paper (downloaded) is silent on stress. The one unheld item (Holmes 2014, other dialect, not openly available) could at most refine, not overturn, the record.

sources.quote: None. The article is a sociolinguistic/language-context profile; it notes vowel differences between the Malua Bay and Espiegles Bay varieties and that 'a detailed study of the phonological relationship between the two varieties is much needed' (p.157), and that a larger grammatical study led by Barbour is under way (p.156).
sources.locator: whole article (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing); phonology remarks limited to comparative vowel correspondences Malua Bay vs Espiegles Bay, Table 1, pp. 156-157
